edges.effect_quant: This is one of the stronger intergenerational obesity signals in the literature. A 2019 individual participant data meta-analysis found maternal obesity associated with an OR of 4.47 for overweight or obesity in late childhood, and a 2013 meta-analysis reported an OR of 3.06 for subsequent offspring overweight or obesity compared with normal-weight mothers.
edges.population: children born to mothers who were obese before or in early pregnancy
edges.mechanism: Maternal obesity can alter the in utero metabolic environment through hyperglycemia, inflammation, insulin resistance, and excess nutrient delivery, while also clustering with postnatal behavioral and genetic influences that reinforce later adiposity in the child.
edges.summary: The literature consistently points toward higher childhood obesity risk after maternal obesity. Across large meta-analyses and cohort data, the association is graded by maternal BMI severity and appears strongest as children age into later childhood.
edges.caveats: Some of the observed effect probably reflects shared family genetics, feeding patterns, and home environment rather than a purely intrauterine mechanism. Even so, the association is strong enough across designs that the overall harmful direction is difficult to dismiss.

evidence.citation: Voerman E et al 2019 PLoS Med
evidence.notes: Maternal body mass index, gestational weight gain, and the risk of overweight and obesity across childhood: An individual participant data meta-analysis.

effect_quant.comparator: late-childhood overweight or obesity in offspring of mothers with obesity versus normal-weight mothers

evidence.notes: Pre-pregnancy body mass index in relation to infant birth weight and offspring overweight/obesity: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
